Landing.metaTitle: Elmorf — Build domain models from data
Landing.metaDescription: Elmorf compiles documents and structured data into a persistent domain model without requiring a predefined schema, ontology or relationship map.
Landing.signInDemo: Sign in to the demo workspace
Landing.heroNoSchema: No schema, ontology or entity definitions required upfront.
Landing.support: Elmorf takes documents and structured data as they are, finds the entities, attributes and relationships in them, and compiles a domain model your software can use.
Landing.proofLine: Load data. Compile it. Get a model.
Landing.transformationTitle: Files stay files. Data becomes a model.
Landing.transformationBody: Elmorf does not ask you to remodel PDFs, spreadsheets, and documents first. It compiles versioned objects, relations, and evidence from them.
Landing.proofTitle: From query to object, relation, and source line.
Landing.proofBody: Elmorf does not hide where an answer came from. Invoice INV-2041 is linked to agreement MSA-1842, and the assertion leads back to the file it was compiled from.
Landing.proofTrace: The source stays attached to the fact
Landing.whatBody: A compiler for records that do not agree with each other. Sources stay files. The compiled model is what your code queries.
Landing.whatExample: Harbor & Pine Supplies — signed — MSA-1842. The evidence stays in the source file.
Landing.loadBody: Bring in the files you already have. Elmorf does not ask you to remodel them first.
Landing.compileBody: Names vary. Records repeat. Values conflict. Relationships are scattered across files. Elmorf turns those observations into persistent objects, relations, attributes, conflicts, and evidence.
Landing.getBody: Ask the current model for an object, a table, or a graph, and keep the evidence.
Landing.demoBody: The Vendor Contracts example: five sources become a model, then one query.
Landing.snippet:
import elmorf

project = "vendor-contracts"
elmorf.load(project=project)
elmorf.compile(project=project)
result = elmorf.get(
  project=project,
  query="open invoices",
)
Landing.fictional: Harbor & Pine is a fictional corpus.
Landing.demoHint: Switch Load, Compile, and Get. The panel on the right follows the step.
Landing.useCasesBody: Different data follows one path: the source remains available, the object becomes consistent, and the answer stays inspectable.
Landing.useCaseContractsBody: Recover parties, agreements, invoices and their relationships.
Landing.useCaseContractsHeadline: Know what exists across thousands of agreements.
Landing.useCaseProductsBody: Resolve products, variants and supplier records into one model.
Landing.useCaseProductsHeadline: Turn conflicting catalogs into one product world.
Landing.useCaseCrmBody: Collapse duplicate people and companies without throwing away the rows that disagreed.
Landing.useCaseEntitiesBody: Decide which records are the same object, and which only look similar.
Landing.useCaseKnowledgeBody: Give later queries one model instead of a pile of spreadsheets.
Landing.useCaseReconcileBody: Connect the same business objects across documents and systems.
Landing.useCaseReconcileHeadline: Connect facts that live in different systems.
Landing.finalEyebrow: You don't have to imagine it
Landing.tryTitle: Open the model that is already compiled.
Landing.tryBody: Vendor Contracts is a fixed corpus on the try page: prepared sources, the compiled model, morphology, and a query. No account.
Landing.tryPageBody: Vendor Contracts is already compiled. Open an object, read its evidence, and run a query. This page does not create an account.
Landing.ownData: Sign in to the demo workspace
Landing.footerNote: Theme and language stay in this browser.
Landing.footerTagline: You provide the data. Elmorf builds the model.
Landing.apiBody: Load the data you already have. Compile it once. Work with the resulting model from code.
Landing.filesBody: PDFs stay PDFs. Spreadsheets stay spreadsheets. APIs stay APIs. Elmorf compiles a model above the sources instead of forcing the sources into one new container.
Landing.filesSecondary: Files stay files. Data becomes a model.
Landing.compileIdentityBody: Recognize when different records describe the same object.
Landing.compileRelationsBody: Recover connections scattered across documents and systems.
Landing.compileAttributesBody: Attach observations to persistent objects instead of isolated chunks.
Landing.compileConflictsBody: Keep incompatible values visible instead of silently picking one.
Landing.compileEvidenceBody: Preserve where every compiled fact came from.
Landing.compileConflictBody: Two effective dates were extracted for MSA-1842.
Landing.modelBody: Objects have identity. Relationships are explicit. Attributes are reconciled. Conflicts stay inspectable. Every fact can point back to evidence.
Landing.provenanceBody: A compiled value is never just a value. Elmorf keeps the path back to the source observation that produced it.
Landing.softwareBody: Applications and agents can work with known objects and relationships instead of rebuilding context from retrieved text on every request.
Landing.softwareNote: The model is compiled once and reused many times.
Landing.pauseModel: A compiled model of the domain.
Landing.finalBody: Open the Vendor Contracts demo and inspect the original sources, objects, relationships, conflicts and evidence.
Landing.schemaBody: Schema-first systems ask you to describe the domain before the data can fit. Elmorf makes the model the result.
Landing.compileLead: Observations become objects, attributes, relations and evidence.
Landing.llmTitle: Why not just give the document to an LLM?
Landing.llmBody: You can. An LLM can extract a structure from a document. Elmorf computes the domain model itself without requiring you to define the target structure first.
Landing.observationsLine: Once ingested, Elmorf works with observations, not file formats.
Landing.llmAgain: new document → new inference → new output
Landing.llmStateLead: An LLM produces a result for an input.
Landing.llmStateTail: Elmorf maintains state across many inputs.
Landing.useCaseAiBody: Give AI structured domain context instead of rebuilding it from raw documents.
Landing.cookieBody: Elmorf stores your language in a cookie so the site stays in the language you chose. The color scheme stays in this browser. There are no analytics or advertising cookies.
Landing.cookieNecessaryBody: This cookie keeps the language you picked. It stays on.

Legal.privacyLead: What this site stores in your browser. The Vendor Contracts corpus is fictional.
Legal.privacyLanguageBody: A cookie named ELMORF_LOCALE stores the language you choose, so the next visit opens in that language.
Legal.privacyThemeBody: Light, dark, or system is saved in this browser. It is not a cookie, and it is not sent to a server.
Legal.privacyTrackingBody: This site does not set analytics or advertising cookies, and it does not sell data.
Legal.privacyAccountBody: Sign-in opens the Harbor & Pine demo in the application. That workspace is separate from these pages.
Legal.termsLead: The public site and the Vendor Contracts corpus are a demonstration.
Legal.termsDemoBody: You can open the compiled model, read evidence, and run a query without an account. The companies and files are fictional.
Legal.termsAccountBody: Signing in enters the demo workspace. This version does not create a separate production account.
Legal.termsChangeBody: The demonstration can change or be reset. Do not use it for real records.
